newFindings.use: research lead only, no kinship claim

newFindings.finding: The three posthumous books were entered as one package on the last day of the legal year 1682/3; 'Vollume 1st' and '2nd vollume' are separate entries, so the two-folio structure is a registration fact; the register calls him 'Batchelor in divinity, and sometimes fellow of New Colledge in Oxford' - a corporate (not booksellers') witness independent of Wood, though not an act of degree.
newFindings.use: dated scene for the editorial-history paragraph; corroborates N-03 and the New College/B.D. attribution; does not supply a degree date (BCD-04/CONFLICT-13 distinction stands)
newFindings.status: ACCEPT (source read); BCD-04 date question unaffected

newFindings.finding: Reid (1853, ii.202) calls Charnock 'a fellow of the college' in the Dublin context (i.e. Trinity College Dublin) - a version found neither in Wood (New College, Oxford) nor in M'Cosh.
newFindings.use: do NOT use to settle any Dublin fellowship question; no college act cited. Article should omit it.
